newsitem.title: UK: Britain's NAAFI says change means 2,000 jobs to go.
newsitem.headline: Britain's NAAFI says change means 2,000 jobs to go.

text.p: Britain's traditional provider of shops, clubs and canteens for its military forces will slim down sharply with the loss of 2,000 jobs after a restructuring and the loss of a major food supply contract, it said on Tuesday.

The Navy, Army and Air Force Institute, known as Naafi, said in a statement that "the consequence of these changes, taken together with the loss of the Ministry of Defence food supply contract, means that the number of employees required to service the new business is significantly reduced."
The 2,000 staff affected will be at Amesbury in south-west England, Nottingham in central England and Kempen in Germany.
"The decision to restructure Naafi has been taken after a thorough review into its future role given the changing climate within which we operate," chief executive Geoffrey Dart said.
Naafi would now concentrate on trading profitably and in particular on its core activities of operating convenience stores and clubs for service personnel and their families.
Increasingly, these activities are being done in partnership with well-known British retailers and leading breweries, it said.
Earlier, the defence ministry said it had placed a new five-year food supply contract worth more than 400 million stg with Booker Plc, switching it away from the Naafi.
